scope: rust-RCP is a software library component used in road-vehicle zonal-architecture ECUs. This TARA covers cybersecurity threats arising from rust-RCP's Command/Response/Status control-plane surface (wire framing, E2E safe-point CRC-32 integrity, authorization policy, rate limiting, priority scheduling, and the UDP/TLS transport bridges) when integrated into a central HPC or zone controller that exchanges RCP frames over an in-vehicle network. System-level CAL may differ after architectural decomposition per ISO/SAE 21434 clause 15.

assets.name: Wire frame structural integrity
assets.description: Correctness of the 16-byte wire header (magic, protocol version, message type, zone, ID/seq, payload length) as decoded by wire::validate_header() and the UDP/TLS bridges

assets.name: E2E safe-point CRC-32 payload integrity
assets.description: Guarantee that a safe-point AVTPDU/ACF frame accepted after crate::request::check_rx_enforce_e2e's TC18 CRC-32 (crate::e2e::crc32_tc18) comparison carries an unmodified payload. Note: as of Milestone 9's e2e REPLACE cutover (ROADMAP.md), this crate no longer has a live anti-replay mechanism (the legacy ReplayGuard sliding window was removed, and evaluate_rx_enforce_seq/REQ-SEQENF-003 is not yet wired into a request-acceptance path), so this asset no longer includes a non-replayed-sender guarantee

assets.name: Zone controller command-execution availability
assets.description: Timely dispatch of Watchdog/Reset/Sleep/Wake commands to the correct zone controller; a delayed or suppressed safety-relevant command can mask a real failure condition

assets.name: Authorization policy enforcement
assets.description: authz::Policy allowlist correctly restricts which (endpoint-type, request-type) pairs a caller may dispatch to a given endpoint — retargeted by Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget from the deleted CommandType/priority key space

assets.name: Rate-limiter and execution-priority availability
assets.description: ratelimit::RateLimitEndpoint remains responsive under sustained load (uniform per-call token-bucket admission, with no Critical-priority exemption since Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget — see T-RCP-04). Note: prioqueue::PrioController was deleted outright by Milestone 9's DEPRECATE-disposition removal (ROADMAP.md Satellite Package Disposition); request::execution_priority_tier/select_next_pending_request (REQ-PRIO-004) is the closest surviving analog but is not yet wired into any dispatch loop, so this asset no longer includes a live guarantee of Critical-priority responsiveness under load

assets.name: Transport confidentiality/authenticity (TLS bridge)
assets.description: tlstransport::TlsBridge enforces TLS 1.2+ and mutual authentication so that wire frames are not exposed to, or accepted from, an unauthenticated peer

threatScenarios.title: Frame injection — bad magic, version, or truncated header
threatScenarios.description: An attacker on the RCP transport (UDP or an unauthenticated TLS peer) sends malformed wire frames — truncated below the 16-byte header, wrong magic bytes, or an unsupported protocol version — attempting to desynchronize the receiver or trigger undefined decode behaviour.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker gains network access to the UDP/TLS transport; crafts a raw byte sequence shorter than HEADER_LEN, or with magic bytes other than 'RC', or ProtoVer != 0x01; sends it before any application-level filtering.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: Low — validate_header() is the mandatory gate before any frame is decoded; ShortFrame/BadMagic/BadVersion are returned instead of panicking

threatScenarios.title: Payload tampering over unauthenticated UDP transport
threatScenarios.description: UDP provides no authentication or encryption. An attacker on the same network segment intercepts a wire frame in transit and modifies the payload bytes (e.g. a Set command's actuation value) before it reaches the zone controller.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker performs ARP spoofing or otherwise gains a man-in-the-middle position on the CAN-to-Ethernet gateway segment carrying RCP-over-UDP; captures a frame; edits payload bytes; re-computes/forges the E2E CRC (see T-RCP-07); re-injects.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: Medium on plain UDP — deployments carrying safety-relevant commands MUST use the TLS bridge (mutual auth, TLS >= 1.2); UDP-only deployments rely solely on the non-cryptographic E2E CRC-32 safe-point check

threatScenarios.title: Replayed command re-injection
threatScenarios.description: An attacker records a previously valid safe-point frame (e.g. a Wake- or Reset-carrying request) and re-transmits it later to re-trigger the action outside its intended context.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker passively captures a genuine wire frame from the transport; re-sends the identical bytes at a time of their choosing.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: Medium — this crate's legacy seqNum/ReplayGuard replay window was removed outright by Milestone 9's e2e REPLACE cutover (ROADMAP.md Satellite Package Disposition), and crate::request::evaluate_rx_enforce_seq/REQ-SEQENF-003's rx_enforce_seq monotonic-sequence check is, as of this item, additive standalone plumbing rather than a mechanism wired into a live request-acceptance path — so no rust-RCP-internal replay protection is currently enforced end-to-end; running RCP over the mutually authenticated TLS bridge (REQ-TLS-001/002) is the primary real-world mitigation until a live rx_enforce_seq integration lands

threatScenarios.title: Command flooding — priority-inversion denial of service
threatScenarios.description: An attacker (or a malfunctioning peer) floods a zone controller with a high volume of Normal/High-priority commands, attempting to starve or delay Critical-priority commands such as Watchdog or Reset.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker gains send access to a zone controller's transport; issues Set/Get commands as fast as the transport allows, with no rate limiting in front of the controller.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: High — ratelimit::RateLimitEndpoint's own token bucket (REQ-RL-006) applies uniformly with no Critical-priority exemption of its own (Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget retired the old REQ-RL-007 carve-out, since Endpoint requests carry no Priority field at all); prioqueue::PrioController (REQ-PQ-004) was deleted outright by Milestone 9's DEPRECATE-disposition removal (ROADMAP.md Satellite Package Disposition), so mitigation against a flood starving genuinely critical requests no longer has any live dispatch-ordering mechanism to depend on. request::execution_priority_tier/select_next_pending_request (REQ-PRIO-004) is the closest surviving analog but remains additive standalone plumbing, not wired into any dispatch loop. A deployment that composes only ratelimit today has no protection against this scenario, and no deployment currently has a live priority-aware one either

threatScenarios.title: Unauthorized safety-relevant command execution
threatScenarios.description: A caller without the intended authority sends a Reset, Sleep, or Wake command to a zone controller that should only accept Get/Set from that caller, attempting to force an unintended power-state transition.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker (or a compromised, lower-trust peer) obtains network access to a zone controller that is composed without an ACL wrapper, or whose Policy allowlist was misconfigured to allow_all(); sends a Reset/Sleep/Wake Command directly. Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget replaced authz::AuthzController (a Controller-wrapping ACL) with authz::AuthzEndpoint (an Endpoint-wrapping ACL keyed on (ep_type, is_write) instead of CommandType) — see that module's own doc comment — so this exact Command-shaped attack against a legacy Controller now has no in-crate ACL wrapper available to compose against it at all, until Milestone 10's core-surface cutover replaces Controller/Command with the endpoint-addressed model authz::AuthzEndpoint already protects.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: High for a deployment still composing a legacy Controller-based zone controller: authz no longer offers a Controller-wrapping ACL at all (that capability was retargeted to authz::AuthzEndpoint, an Endpoint-space ACL, by Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget), so this exact Command-shaped attack has no in-crate mitigation until Milestone 10 replaces the Controller/Command surface itself. For the new Endpoint-space surface, residual risk remains deployment-dependent as before: the ACL is enforced only when the integrator wraps every externally reachable Endpoint in an AuthzEndpoint with a least-privilege Policy; rust-RCP cannot force composition at the library level

threatScenarios.title: TLS downgrade or missing peer authentication
threatScenarios.description: An attacker forces (or a misconfigured deployment permits) a TLS session below TLSv1.2, or a peer without a valid client certificate, allowing eavesdropping or impersonation of a zone controller/HPC endpoint.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker performs a protocol-downgrade attack against the TLS handshake, or connects to a TlsBridge whose injected TlsStream implementation does not actually enforce mutual authentication despite REQUIRE_MUTUAL_AUTH being declared true.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: Low in-library — MIN_TLS_VERSION/REQUIRE_MUTUAL_AUTH are the declared policy constants; actual enforcement depends on the concrete TlsStream implementation the integrator injects, which rust-RCP does not itself provide or audit

threatScenarios.title: E2E CRC forgery — active tampering by a capable attacker
threatScenarios.description: The E2E safe-point check uses the OPEN Alliance TC18 CRC-32 (polynomial 0xF4ACFB13), which is a safety control against random bit errors, not a keyed cryptographic MAC. An attacker who can modify a frame in transit can recompute a valid CRC-32 over the tampered coverage buffer, defeating the check.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker intercepts a wire frame (see T-RCP-02); modifies the payload; recomputes the CRC-32 safe-point value over the new coverage buffer bytes (no key material required — the algorithm and polynomial are public, per the OPEN Alliance TC18 Remote Control Protocol Specification); re-injects the forged frame.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: Medium-High without transport-layer authentication — the e2e::crc32_tc18-based safe-point check MUST be documented as a safety control (random error detection) only, not a security control; deployments exposed to an adversarial network MUST run RCP over the TLS bridge (mutually authenticated) rather than relying on the CRC-32 safe-point check alone

threatScenarios.title: Watchdog suppression masking loss of supervision
threatScenarios.description: Per the per-stream liveness-reset-on-every-request watchdog model (watchdog::StreamWatchdogState/evaluate_stream_watchdog, ROADMAP.md Milestone 6), an attacker injects or replays forged requests against a stream at less than its rx_wd_timeout_interval cadence, keeping StreamWatchdogState::reset_on_request firing and evaluate_stream_watchdog reporting StreamWatchdogOutcome::Alive even though the stream's real endpoint(s) have failed.
threatScenarios.attackPath: Attacker with transport-level injection capability (see T-RCP-02) sends forged or replayed requests on the target stream's own identifier at a rate that keeps resetting its watchdog liveness, suppressing the ExpiredNoSafestate/ExpiredSafestate outcome evaluate_stream_watchdog would otherwise report.
threatScenarios.residualRisk: Medium — forging traffic that resets a stream's liveness timer is a transport-layer attack outside rust-RCP's own visibility; running the watchdog path over an authenticated, integrity-protected transport (TLS bridge, mutual auth) is the primary mitigation, since the library cannot itself distinguish a genuine request from a forged one without it

cybersecurityGoals.description: rust-RCP shall reject all wire frames with a structurally invalid header (short, bad magic, or unsupported protocol version) before any field is interpreted.

rust-RCP shall provide a mechanism to detect corrupted safe-point Command/Response/Status frames (the TC18 CRC-32 safe-point check), and shall document that neither it nor rx_enforce_seq's monotonic-sequence check (not yet wired into a live request path) provide replay protection or cryptographic integrity/authenticity against an active attacker — that requires running RCP over the mutually authenticated TLS bridge.

rust-RCP shall resist priority-inversion denial-of-service by always dispatching Critical-priority commands ahead of lower-priority traffic, and by admitting no unbounded request flood through ratelimit's own token bucket. Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget of ratelimit dropped its own Critical-priority exemption (Endpoint requests carry no Priority field), and its later DEPRECATE-disposition removal (ROADMAP.md Satellite Package Disposition) deleted prioqueue::PrioController outright. request::execution_priority_tier/select_next_pending_request (REQ-PRIO-004) is the closest surviving analog — built ahead of schedule in Milestone 5 — but remains additive standalone plumbing not wired into any dispatch loop, so this goal is not presently satisfied by any live mechanism; flagged as an open gap for whichever later item wires REQ-PRIO-004 into live dispatch.

rust-RCP shall provide an authorization allowlist that integrators can compose in front of any Endpoint to restrict which (endpoint-type, request-type) pairs a caller may dispatch, and a per-stream watchdog mechanism whose liveness-reset and safe-state-on-expiry behavior is independently verifiable. Milestone 9's ADAPT retarget moved this allowlist from wrapping Controller (keyed on CommandType) to wrapping Endpoint (keyed on (ep_type, is_write)) — see T-RCP-05's own residualRisk for the resulting Controller-space coverage gap.
rust-RCP's TLS bridge shall declare and enforce a minimum TLS version of 1.2 and mandatory mutual authentication for any transport carrying safety-relevant commands.
